chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:

A son of one of the companions of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) died, so Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) attended. When he was placed in the grave niche, his father stepped forward and threw soil upon him. Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) took his hands and said: 'Do not throw soil upon him, and whoever is a close relative of his should not throw soil upon him, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the parent or one with womb relationships from throwing soil upon their deceased.'

So we said: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, are you forbidding us from this alone?' He said: 'I am forbidding you from throwing soil upon your close relatives, for that causes hardness in the heart, and whoever is hard of heart is distant from his Lord.'
ai.seo_question: Why should parents not throw soil on the deceased according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links the physical act of burial to spiritual psychology, warning that parents throwing soil may develop 'hardness of the heart' (qasawat al-qalb), a state of emotional detachment that distances one from God. This ruling is rooted in the Prophet’s prohibition and is interpreted by Shia scholars as preserving the natural tenderness of kinship, preventing the ritual from becoming a mechanical act that dulls emotional sensitivity.
